history.reason: Both rows are built on the granary, an objective the GDD deleted on 2026-08-14; the deterministic lint proves this on both rows and caps them. Prompts_01_FirstSightGranary names a nonexistent objective in its trigger ("FirstSight.Granary"), its bark ("Their whole winter sleeps in that shed, goblin. Wake it.") and its HUD line ("Granary — burn it: one of three targets done. Torch: Q"); the required trio is Market / Statue / Windmill (GDD§2.8#5), so this row must be retargeted at one of those three — e.g. the market stalls, whose burn is "burn the stalls and you burn the hamlet's livelihood" (GDD§2.8#4). Whispers_04_ObjectiveGranaryStage1FirstT has the same problem plus a structural one: it invents a Stage-1 for the granary, when the only two-stage set piece in the slice is the windmill (Ablaze → window shot → Detonation, GDD§2.8#4). Its bark also chains clauses — "light it and go. The guards are thickest here; that is the tax" — where the format calls for one bark and one HUD line naming objective/payoff/control (GDD§2.8#6); it carries no HUD line at all despite being a FirstTime prompt, so the trio isn't delivered. Beyond the granary, the writing is on-register: no settlement is christened, no fear reaction, no cut-content vocabulary (no Slasher, palisade, Pennybrook), and no audio cue is referenced. The Overlord voice is close but a touch flat — "that is the tax" is dry rather than pompous-and-underwhelmed, and neither line lands the trailing "…adequate" mockery of GDD§2.1#1.

per_rule.quote: Granary — burn it: one of three targets done. Torch: Q
per_rule.required_instead: Deterministic lint finding (granary, removed from the GDD 2026-08-14, queue #156) on both rows — unresolvable by judgement. The required trio is Market / Statue / Windmill; retarget both rows onto one of those three, and note the only two-stage objective is the windmill, so "Objective.Granary.Stage1" has no counterpart to convert to except Objective.Windmill.Stage1.

per_rule.quote: Their whole winter, stacked in one shed — light it and go. The guards are thickest here; that is the tax.
per_rule.required_instead: A first-time prompt is one bark plus ONE HUD line naming exactly three things: objective, payoff, and the one control. This row is a FirstTime trigger with hud_line and control both empty, so the player is told no control at all, and the bark chains an extra clause ("The guards are thickest here; that is the tax"). Cut the trailing clause and supply a ≤90-char HUD line, e.g. the shape used in Prompts_01. Prompts_01's own HUD line is well-formed at 53 chars (objective / payoff "one of three targets done" / control "Torch: Q").

per_rule.quote: The guards are thickest here; that is the tax.
per_rule.required_instead: Register is right — whispered, proprietary, unimpressed, not grimdark assassin menace — but this lands dry and tactical rather than pompous-gravitas-over-petty-theft, and neither row reaches for the mockery of GDD§2.1#1 ("I have seen rats do better. …adequate."). Minor drift only; "Their whole winter sleeps in that shed, goblin. Wake it." is genuinely on-voice.

history.reason: Both rows are keyed to a granary that no longer exists — the deterministic lint finding fires on both trigger ids ("FirstSight.Granary" and "Objective.Granary.Stage1.FirstTime"), and the GDD removed the granary on 2026-08-14; the required trio is Market / Statue / Windmill (GDD§2.8#5). That lint is proven and caps VOCAB_SLICE at 6 regardless of the body text, which does otherwise describe legitimate slice content (market stalls, windmill two-stage). Fix by re-keying the triggers to FirstSight.Market and Objective.Windmill.Stage1.FirstTime. Beyond that, both HUD lines break FORMAT_PROMPT by naming a second thing beyond the required three: row FirstSight.Granary's "Market — burn the stalls: one of three targets done. Torch: Q" pads with a progress-counter clause instead of a clean objective/payoff/control triple, and row Objective.Granary.Stage1.FirstTime's "Windmill: Ablaze — a window shot detonates it. Aimed throw: RMB + Q" names two controls ("RMB + Q") where the guide requires the ONE control that does it (GDD§2.8#5) — the GDD's own line is "Windmill: Ablaze — needs a window shot." Both are under 90 characters. Tone is good: "…adequate" lands the Overlord register (GDD§2.1#1), the windmill bark is near-verbatim canon, and "the town is impressed. I am not" is mockery, not mourning. No settlement is named, no non-slice vocabulary appears, and nothing references audio.

per_rule.required_instead: The granary was deleted from the GDD on 2026-08-14; the required trio is Market / Statue / Windmill. Re-key the triggers to FirstSight.Market and Objective.Windmill.Stage1.FirstTime.

per_rule.quote: Windmill: Ablaze — a window shot detonates it. Aimed throw: RMB + Q
per_rule.required_instead: Exactly three things and ONE control. "RMB + Q" is a second control; the FirstSight row also adds a fourth element ("one of three targets done"). Write e.g. "Windmill: Ablaze — a window shot detonates it. Aimed throw: RMB" and "Market — burn the stalls, gut their livelihood. Torch: Q".

history.reason: Both rows are close to shipped quality: the market bark and the windmill Stage-1 bark carry the Overlord's whispered, underwhelmed register (GDD§2.1#1, GDD§2.8#4), both HUD lines are well under 90 characters and name exactly the objective, the payoff and one control, and nothing references a voice file, SFX or sound. Two actionable drifts. (1) Row 1 (FirstSight.Market) is tagged "speaker": "HUD" while its text is plainly an Overlord bark — "The stalls, goblin. Their whole livelihood, stacked in wicker and waiting. Light it. …adequate." The prompt system in GDD§2.8#5 is one bark from His Eternal Darkness PLUS one HUD note; the bark row must be speaker "Overlord" (as row 2 correctly is), with the hud_line as the separate HUD element. Fix the speaker field; the wording itself is fine. (2) Row 2 (Objective.Windmill.Stage1.FirstTime) adds "and the town is impressed" to the canon bark. Per GDD§2.10#0 the hamlet's reaction to arson is denial, not admiration — the town mutters "must've been a badger" and keeps pottering. Either drop the clause back to the canon line ("Her skin's alight, goblin, but it's the dust in her belly that'll bring her down — put fire through a window") or replace it with a denial beat the Overlord can sneer at, e.g. "and they're still calling it a badger. I am not impressed." No settlement is named, no out-of-slice content (no granary, no Slasher, no palisade, no Pennybrook) appears, and the statue is not invoked as burnable.

per_rule.quote: Her skin's alight, goblin, and the town is impressed.

per_rule.quote: "speaker": "HUD", "text": "The stalls, goblin. Their whole livelihood, stacked in wicker and waiting. Light it. …adequate."

history.reason: Both rows read as shipped Tier-1 Goblin Siege content. Row 1 (FirstSight.Market) uses only slice vocabulary — market stalls, torch — and its HUD line "Market — burn the stalls, gut their livelihood. Torch: Q" (55 chars) names exactly the objective (market), the payoff (their livelihood), and one control (Q), matching GDD§2.8#5's three-part prompt spec and GDD§2.8#4's "burn the stalls and you burn the hamlet's livelihood." Row 2 (Objective.Windmill.Stage1.FirstTime) is a faithful variant of the canon Stage-1 bark in GDD§2.8#4, and its added clause "and they're still calling it a badger" lands the disbelief joke of GDD§2.10#0 rather than fear — no 'run for your lives' register anywhere. Its HUD line "Windmill: Ablaze — a window shot detonates it. Aimed throw: RMB" (62 chars) again names objective, payoff, and one control, with the aimed throw exactly as canon requires. Neither row names the hamlet (GDD§2.8#6: settlements stay nameless), neither mentions granary, palisade, Slasher, Brute, Pennybrook or Silverford, neither burns the statue, and neither references a voice line, SFX cue or sound — barks are text-only. No deterministic lint findings were reported. The one soft spot is TONE_OVERLORD in row 1: "Light it. …adequate." attaches the trailing "…adequate" to an order the player has not yet carried out, whereas GDD§2.1#1 uses it as a whispered *verdict* on work already done ("Adequate. I have seen rats do better. …adequate."). A rewriter should either withhold the sign-off until there is something to be underwhelmed by, or aim the underwhelm at the target rather than the unperformed act — e.g. "The stalls, goblin. Their whole livelihood, stacked in wicker and waiting. Barely worth the flame. Light it." Everything else is on-brand; do not change it.

per_rule.required_instead: The trailing '…adequate' is a verdict on work already done (GDD§2.1#1), not a sign-off on an order just given; either hold it back or point the underwhelm at the target — e.g. 'Their whole livelihood, stacked in wicker. Barely worth the flame. Light it.'
